entities.name: Euneas
entities.description: A Meletian who dreams of the city's plaza being crushed under endless replacement columns and consumed by grime.

entities.name: Pollio
entities.description: A metalworker of Akros with a wife and children who dreams of being bound with the city's twine into one mass of flesh.

entities.name: Melantha
entities.description: A priestess of Ephara and member of the high council who dreams of her old mentor Xenocrates, whom she saw poisoned.

entities.name: Xenocrates
entities.description: An early mentor of Melantha at Ephara's temple who appears in her dream, coughing blood and speaking forbidden theories about the gods.

entities.name: Koblios
entities.description: Author of Meditations who said the gods are simply patterns personified and was stoned for heresy.

entities.name: Tomakri
entities.description: A baker of Akros who makes the sweet cinnamon rolls Pollio's wife loves.

entities.name: Kopaknios
entities.description: An ingot-deliverer who supplies the metals Pollio works.

entities.name: Ashiok
entities.description: A planeswalker dream-weaver who created the dreams and the god Cacophony as an artistic display, hiding from the gods with a boon from Phenax.

entities.name: Cacophony
entities.description: A short-lived god of cities that awakens from the city's dream and is destroyed by Ephara.

entities.name: Ephara
entities.description: A god, shown as a tall dark-skinned woman covered in the stars of Nyx, who destroys Cacophony.

entities.name: Phenax
entities.description: A god who granted Ashiok a temporary boon of concealment, warning against harming a god.

entities.name: Xenagos
entities.description: A planeswalker who turned a mortal into a god and whose fascination with godhood mystifies Ashiok.

entities.name: Heliod
entities.description: A god whose earliest writings Xenocrates cites.

entities.name: Thassa
entities.description: A god whose earliest writings Xenocrates cites.

entities.name: Meletis
entities.description: The polis of scholars and philosophers whose plaza appears in Euneas's dream.

entities.name: Akros
entities.description: The city whose crowded streets appear in Pollio's dream.

entities.name: Theros
entities.description: The plane where gods are shaped by mortals' patterns and where Ashiok hides from the gods.

entities.name: Nyx
entities.description: The divine realm through whose power, Xenocrates says, mortals create their gods.

entities.name: Temple of Ephara
entities.description: A temple to Ephara, one of which in a deserted city is where Ashiok creates Cacophony.

events.summary: In a dream, Euneas watches the Meletian plaza crushed beneath endless replacement columns until the city swallows him whole; he wakes screaming.
events.quote: The city had claimed him whole, another piece of sediment for the streets future inhabitants would trod upon in their brief doomed hours.

events.summary: In a dream, Pollio ties twine to his family, customers and friends until the ropes grow tight and the crowd's flesh knits into a single mass; he wakes screaming.
events.quote: Then, Pollio was part of one amorphous mass of stinking flesh and burning rope

events.summary: In a dream, Melantha dines with her dead mentor Xenocrates, who drinks wine from a poisoned goblet and coughs up blood as he voices blasphemous theories; she wakes screaming.
events.quote: I did not... I did not kill you, Xenocrates.

events.summary: Xenocrates argues that gods are the patterns mortals recognize, personified through the power of Nyx, and that mortals are responsible for their gods; Melantha forbids it as blasphemy.
events.quote: Through the power of Nyx, we are responsible for our gods.

events.summary: In a city's dream, small hairy creatures overrun a content, resting city, which is driven to awaken by a voice.
events.quote: Every avenue and structure of the city was covered with the hairy pests

events.summary: The city awakens as Cacophony, god of cities, and begins crushing the ape-like humans clinging to its body.
events.quote: Cacophony, the god of cities, arose.

events.summary: Ephara appears, calls Cacophony a monstrosity and plunges her hands into it, draining its life; the god of cities never wakes again.
events.quote: Cacophony, the god of cities dark, never woke again.

events.summary: Ashiok, whose concealment from Phenax's boon fades, reveals that they sculpted the dreams to create the god Cacophony as a display, hiding in an abandoned Ephara temple.
events.quote: The earth's rumbles faded to stillness as the last remnant of Phenax's glamour dissolved around Ashiok.

events.summary: Ashiok recalls repaying a favor to Phenax with a boon to hide from the gods, and Phenax's warning not to use it to harm a god.
events.quote: The boon was a temporary one, and Phenax had been very explicit about Ashiok's fate if Ashiok used the boon to attempt to injure or murder a god.

events.summary: Ashiok reflects that turning an idea into a god is easy compared to Xenagos's feat, and that Cacophony could rise again.
events.quote: But turning an idea into a god was much easier.

relations.note: Ephara drains Cacophony's life and it never wakes.
relations.quote: I am Ephara, and you should no more exist than a finger separated from its hand.

relations.note: Ashiok shaped the city-dream that became the god Cacophony.
relations.quote: But Phenax had never said anything about attempting to create a new god.

relations.note: Phenax owed Ashiok a favor and granted a boon of concealment from the gods.
relations.quote: to repay a favor the Planeswalker had done for the god.

relations.note: Xenocrates was one of her first mentors at Ephara's temple.
relations.quote: Xenocrates had been one of her first mentors at Ephara's temple

relations.note: Melantha is a priestess of Ephara's temple and on the high council.
relations.quote: to balance the demands of serving her god with finding acceptance among her peers
